title: Extra Characters in a String
pattern: DP on String with Trie Matching
spaceBreakdown:
- trie nodes (vector<array<int,26>>): up to D·L nodes, each 26 ints → O(D·L)
- isEnd vector: up to D·L entries → O(D·L)
- dp vector: n+1 ints → O(n)
- recursion depth: none (iterative)
- not counted: input string s, input dictionary
approach: Build a trie from the dictionary. Define dp[i] = minimum extra characters when optimally breaking s[0:i]. For each start position i, either leave s[i] as extra (dp[i+1] = dp[i]+1) or, by walking the trie from position i forward, every time a word ends at position j, relax dp[j+1] = min(dp[j+1], dp[i]). The trie lets each start position match all dictionary words in O(L) total instead of iterating every word, giving O(n·L) time.
hints: When scanning s left to right, at each position you either leave the current character unused or start a dictionary word there. What does the optimal decision at position i depend on from the part of s you've already processed? s.length ≤ 50.

Use dynamic programming with a trie. dp[i] = min extra chars for prefix s[0:i]; from each start i, walk the trie along s[i..] and, whenever a word ends at j, relax dp[j+1] with dp[i]. For "leetscode" starting at i=0, the trie walk hits "leet" ending at j=3, so dp[4] becomes dp[0]=0.

build trie from dictionary
dp[0] = 0, dp[1..n] = INF
for i in 0..n-1:
    dp[i+1] = min(dp[i+1], dp[i] + 1)        # leave s[i] extra
    node = root
    for j in i..n-1:
        node = trie.child(node, s[j])
        if node is null: break
        if node is word end:
            dp[j+1] = min(dp[j+1], dp[i])
return dp[n]

**Smallest input** - single character not in dictionary.
`Input: s = "a", dictionary = ["b"]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: initialising dp with 0 instead of INF and only relaxing via word matches → returns 0.

**Whole string is one word** - the trie walk must continue past the first word end to catch longer words.
`Input: s = "leetcode", dictionary = ["leet","leetcode"]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: breaking out of the trie walk on the first isEnd instead of continuing → dp[4]=0 but dp[8] stays INF, returns 4.

**No character matches any word** - every position must fall through to the "+1" branch.
`Input: s = "xyz", dictionary = ["abc"]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: forgetting the dp[i+1] = dp[i]+1 relaxation → dp stays INF, returns garbage/INF.

**Overlapping word choices** - shorter word leaves extra chars that a longer word avoids.
`Input: s = "leetscode", dictionary = ["leet","code","leetcode"]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: greedily taking the first matched word "leet" then failing to also try starting fresh at i=4 → returns 5 instead of 1.

followUps.q: What if s.length can be up to 10^5 and dictionary up to 10^5 words of length up to 10^5?
followUps.a: The trie-based DP still works in O(n·L) where L is the max word length, but L could be 10^5. Cap the inner walk at the maximum dictionary word length stored during trie build, so each start position does at most L work; total O(n·L) time, O(D·L) space.

followUps.q: What if dictionary words can be added and removed between queries on the same s?
followUps.a: Keep the trie persistent and support insert/delete by maintaining a per-node count of words ending there; each query reruns the O(n·L) DP. With Q queries total time is O(Q·n·L), space stays O(D·L + n).

followUps.q: What if s arrives as a streaming character stream and you must report the current minimum extra characters after each new character?
followUps.a: Maintain dp incrementally: when character c arrives at position i, compute dp[i+1] from dp[i]+1 and from all word ends reachable by walking the trie backward from i. To avoid O(L) per character, store for each position the set of active trie states; time O(n·L) total, space O(n·L) for the active-state lists.
